## My request:
so what's the solution here? I wanted clanker to be able to handle payments as well

<image name=[Image #1] path="/var/folders/3k/f45nj0jn3b11jfvyvt0nxj4w0000gn/T/codex-clipboard-b605347a-32a8-4833-8c72-220df474d813.png">

</image>

<image name=[Image #2] path="/var/folders/3k/f45nj0jn3b11jfvyvt0nxj4w0000gn/T/codex-clipboard-6875d49f-6b9d-4ed2-b081-e36d923744a8.png">

</image>

The block is **Clanker’s current implementation and prompts**, not proof that Kernel fundamentally cannot support payments.

1. **Payments are deliberately disabled.** [clanker_policy.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/clanker_policy.py:4) makes payment owner-only. [plugin.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/seatbelt/plugin.py:201) additionally forbids card/CVV collection, approval forms, and purchase submission, including merchant-saved cards. [tools.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/tools.py:7) excludes payment tools, and lines 16–17 reject cached calls. [payments.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/payments.py:5) unconditionally rejects every payment operation.

2. **The earlier payment prototype was removed during Kernel migration.** [local-vault-removal.md](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-08-local-vault-removal.md:6) explicitly lists removed card storage and payment execution. The [October 6 decision](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-06-payment-vault.md:11) describes an owner-bound, one-use approval with final-total validation and receipt checks. That was a local-browser prototype, tested with dummy checkout pages; it never established real merchant payments or supported hosted card iframes/3DS.

3. **The checkout handoff in the screenshots does not exist.** The private sign-in link resolves to Kernel’s active login flow and expires when login finishes: [managed_auth.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:360). Browser creation receives `browser_live_view_url` but retains only a boolean indicating its presence: [kernel_client.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/kernel_client.py:171). Sending the user back to the sign-in message cannot reliably expose the prepared cart.

4. **Kernel’s existing transport could be a building block, but Clanker needs a payment integration.** [kernel_vault_client.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/kernel_vault_client.py:364) fills arbitrary named credential fields into selectors without passing their values through the model. Clanker’s metadata and collection layers currently whitelist login/personal/API-key types: [kernel_store.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/kernel_store.py:207), [kernel_service.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/kernel_service.py:745). Extending those and removing prompt refusals alone would not establish a reliable payment system.

5. **Recommended product flow:** Clanker opens payment options, reports merchant/items/delivery/final total in Slack, obtains purchase-specific approval there, then a backend-controlled payment executor fills an opaque payment handle and submits once. Bind approval to owner, task, checkout, currency and exact amount; invalidate changed totals; consume approval before submission; reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying; require a merchant receipt for success. Start with COD or an existing merchant-saved payment method, then add cards and bank authentication. OTP/3DS/UPI confirmation still needs a supported private/bank approval step.

One additional boundary: the generic browser middleware checks task ownership and privacy, but does not enforce a purchase approval against arbitrary browser clicks: [plugin.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/seatbelt/plugin.py:107). A production payment flow should enforce the final commitment in the executor, beyond prompt instructions.

Read-only audit completed; no files, browser sessions, payments, or Slack state changed.
